gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Microsoft's Windows 11 hardware certification (introduced alongside version 24H2) requires DisplayPort Alt Mode on every USB-C port of a certified laptop, so the "check your port carries video" step the rivals and ChatGPT stop at has a rule behind it on such Windows laptops, while on a Mac the limit is the display count Apple publishes (one external display on an M2 MacBook Air) and macOS mirrors instead of extending over MST.
standout_why: Compared against The Office Journal under-$200 (cited) and under-$150 (cited), itechguides 'Best Laptop Screen Extenders in 2025' (cited in the second chat) and our own under-$300 page (rank 10); deskfinds.com returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The Office Journal says two-screen setups 'usually need two USB-C ports that carry video (DisplayPort Alt Mode or Thunderbolt)' and that base M1–M3 MacBooks have 'limited' support, with no number, no MST and no way to tell whether a port carries video. itechguides says 'USB-C does not automatically mean video' and 'Verify USB-C DisplayPort Alt Mode', with no MST and no Mac display count. Our under-$300 page already has one video connection per screen, the Plugable MST line and Apple's per-model counts, so those parts are not new against the full result list. None of the pages read has the Microsoft certification rule or its 27% figure.
decides: It confirms the split rather than overturning a pick. A single added screen under $200 needs one video-capable USB-C port, which the Microsoft rule covers on every USB-C port of a laptop certified under the 24H2-era program. A driver-free two-screen extender under $200 (FOPO S7 through our link, or the Laptomo dual and Arzopa E1 that ChatGPT showed) needs the laptop to drive two external displays: on a certified Windows laptop with two USB-C ports that is covered by the same rule, but on an M2 MacBook Air Apple's one-external-display limit means only one added screen can extend, and a one-cable MST design would mirror on macOS. So the page should send Mac owners with base chips to a single screen and keep the dual-screen pick for Windows laptops with two video outputs. The rule is no guarantee for laptops certified before 24H2; those owners still have to check the port.

findings.label: Microsoft certification rule for USB-C video on Windows 11 laptops
findings.value: "DisplayPort Alt-Mode is required for all USB-C ports to support connecting monitors."; "USB Data, Charging and Display 'just works' on all USB-C ports"
findings.source_title: Ending USB-C® Port Confusion (Microsoft USB Blog, 30 May 2025, updated 23 Sep 2025)
findings.note: Applies to WHCP-certified mobile PCs; Microsoft says the requirements were introduced "alongside the release of Windows 11, version 24H2". The post does not say an older laptop updated to 24H2 gains anything, so treat it as a rule for laptops certified under that program only. The requirements table in the post is an image and was not readable as text.

findings.label: How often USB-C ports on Windows PCs fall short (Microsoft's figure)
findings.value: 27% of PCs with USB4 have encountered a limited functionality notification
findings.source_title: Ending USB-C® Port Confusion (Microsoft USB Blog)
findings.note: Microsoft cites Windows Diagnostics Data; this is the stated reason for the rule. The notification covers any unsupported USB-C function, not only video.

findings.label: Display requirement for Windows laptops advertising USB 40Gbps or 80Gbps
findings.value: "DisplayPort requirements ensure support for up to two 4K monitors at 60Hz"
findings.source_title: Ending USB-C® Port Confusion (Microsoft USB Blog)
findings.note: Relevant to two-screen extenders: a certified laptop advertising USB 40Gbps is required to drive two external monitors. The post presents this for mobile systems advertising USB 40Gbps or 80Gbps.

findings.label: MST (several displays over one DisplayPort or USB-C output) by operating system
findings.value: Windows: "Fully support MST for extended desktop configurations." macOS: "MST is not supported on macOS for extended displays." and "MST-connected displays are mirrored, not extended."
findings.source_title: Understanding MST: Multi-Display Setups with Windows, macOS, and DisplayPort (Plugable, last updated 26 Mar 2025)
findings.note: Plugable is a dock maker, not Apple. Already quoted on our under-$300 page, so not new against the full result list. Whether any candidate here uses MST inside was not established (see unsourced).
